toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The single high Level 2 potassium result on Analyzer B looks like a one-off. The repeat from the same vial passed within 21 minutes. Levels 1 and 3, sodium and chloride were all fine. Level 2 averages are unchanged since the lot change (5.81 before, 5.80 after). One flag a month is expected by chance at this QC volume. Patient checks agree: 43 samples re-run on Analyzer A differed by +0.02 mmol/L on average, and all were within the allowed difference. The patient median is stable. QC ran on time on all three days, so the staffing and skipped-QC theory isn't supported. I can't tell whether it was a sampling glitch or chance, so I wouldn't record a cause as confirmed.

Ward 6's high potassiums are not from Analyzer B. Half were run on Analyzer A. The tube outage means long transit times, and the renal overflow patients are a second possible explanation. Neither has been separated out yet.

What to sign off: return Analyzer B to potassium service and close the review of the 186 results with no amendments. Add an extra Level 2 QC at the start of each shift for a week. Don't recall results, quarantine the lot or widen the limits. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples, taken without the tube delay, on its high results. Reopen the case if a second QC failure appears.
